chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who made up a day from the month of Ramadan and then had intercourse with his wife. He said: Upon him is the expiation that is upon the one who had intercourse during Ramadan, because that day, in the sight of God, is from the days of Ramadan.

This report came as rare and unusual (shadh), and it can be meant for the one who broke his fast on that day after midday (zuwal) in a manner of轻视 and negligence regarding the obligation of God Almighty, in which case that expiation is obligatory upon him as a strict punishment. As for the one who was not like that, but rather believed that completing the fast was preferable, but desire overcame him and compelled him to break the fast, then only what we have previously mentioned is obligatory upon him.

key_terms.الزّوَال: Midday (when the sun passes its zenith)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for making up a missed Ramadan fast day if one has intercourse on that makeup day?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* addresses the specific legal ruling for a man who, after making up a missed Ramadan fast, engages in intercourse on that makeup day. The narrator highlights the report's rarity (*shadh*) and offers a nuanced interpretation: the full Ramadan expiation applies if the act was done with negligence or contempt for the divine command, whereas mere overwhelming desire without such intent only requires the basic makeup (*qada*). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between the intent behind breaking the fast and the specific timing of the act to determine the severity of the penalty.
